items.stem: GPS events sometimes arrive seconds after they occurred due to network delays. Which concept distinguishes when an event happened from when it is processed?

options.rationale: Correct: event time is when it occurred; processing time is when the pipeline handles it.
Batch size concerns throughput, not timing semantics.
Retention is how long messages are kept, not timing semantics.
Worker count affects capacity, not event vs processing time.

items.explanation: Correct: event time vs processing time captures this distinction.

items.stem: Which TWO help a Dataflow streaming job handle problem messages correctly? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Send unparseable messages to a dead-letter topic
options.rationale: Correct: dead-lettering isolates bad messages without stopping the pipeline.
Correct: idempotency makes reprocessing safe under at-least-once delivery.

options.text: Drop any message that arrives late without recording it
options.rationale: Silently dropping late data loses information and is rarely acceptable.

options.text: Assume exactly-once removes all need for idempotency
options.rationale: Robust pipelines still design for safe reprocessing.

items.explanation: Correct: dead-letter topics and idempotent transforms both improve correctness.

items.stem: You need per-minute counts from a continuous event stream. Which windowing approach fits?

options.rationale: Correct: fixed one-minute windows produce non-overlapping per-minute aggregates.

options.text: A single global window with no trigger
options.rationale: A global window without triggers never emits interim results.
Unbounded streams need windows to aggregate over time.
Per-minute counts on a live stream require streaming windows.

items.explanation: Correct: fixed one-minute windows yield per-minute counts.
